nodes.title: SG-6 · Clean up leftover references to removed code
nodes.body:
Context: the worker, execution backend, config keys, routes and ExecutionPanel are already deleted. Two leftovers remain. game/frontend/src/components/LifecycleStepper.tsx still exports deriveStage and an EXECUTION_STAGES map that only served the removed execution flow, and nothing in src imports deriveStage. The docs say nothing about the handoff: backend/README.md contains only 'hello Worldseed', there is no docs/ folder, and nothing describes the frozen-contribution export. Desired behavior: no code or docs refer to execution state, and the docs describe the handoff to devion workseed. Expected result: backend and frontend tests pass with game/src, the game UI, game/content, backend/internal/contribution and the round lifecycle unchanged. Why: Worldseed is a game and contribution project, not a development platform.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given LifecycleStepper.tsx, when it is read, then it has no deriveStage export and no execution-status mapping, and AdminApp still renders LifecycleStepper from round.status
- Given the backend README and the handoff doc, when they are read, then they describe the handoff of frozen contributions to devion workseed using the Export JSON format
- Given the backend and game/frontend unit test suites, when they run, then they pass


## Scope
- In scope: LifecycleStepper execution helpers
- In scope: Handoff documentation under backend/
- Out of scope: game/src
- Out of scope: game UI components
- Out of scope: game/content
- Out of scope: round lifecycle logic
- Out of scope: contribution package behavior
- Preserve: Export JSON format v1
- Preserve: Existing guard tests for removed code
- Preserve: STAGES and stageIndex behavior


## Technical constraints
- Go backend module and Vitest frontend must stay green
- Do not modify game/src, game/content or backend/internal/contribution non-test code


## Definition of done
- Both requirements are implemented and verified by unit tests
- No execution references remain in LifecycleStepper or docs


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · LifecycleStepper carries no execution-derived stage logic
nodes.body:
Context: LifecycleStepper.tsx exports EXECUTION_STAGES and deriveStage(roundStatus, executionStatus), which map execution statuses to stages. Execution no longer exists and AdminApp only passes round.status. Desired behavior: only STAGES, stageIndex and LifecycleStepper remain. Expected result: the stepper renders the same as before. Why: it removes the last frontend reference to execution state.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given the LifecycleStepper module, when its exports are inspected, then deriveStage is undefined and STAGES, stageIndex and LifecycleStepper are still exported
- Given status CLOSED, when LifecycleStepper renders, then the CLOSED step has aria-current=step and OPEN is done
- Given LifecycleStepper.tsx, when its source is read, then it contains no 'execution' text


## Scope
- In scope: game/frontend/src/components/LifecycleStepper.tsx
- Out of scope: AdminApp layout
- Out of scope: game UI
- Preserve: STAGES order
- Preserve: STATUS_ALIASES
- Preserve: stageIndex


## Technical constraints
- Frontend tsc --noEmit must still pass


## Definition of done
- deriveStage and EXECUTION_STAGES are deleted
- Stepper rendering is unchanged


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · Documentation describes the handoff to devion workseed
nodes.body:
Context: backend/README.md contains only 'hello Worldseed' and no docs describe the handoff. The Export type in backend/internal/contribution/export.go defines JSON v1 with version, world_id, round_id and contributions[id, author, content, created_at], and the Exporter includes only frozen contributions in snapshot order. Desired behavior: the docs say Worldseed collects contributions and hands frozen ones to devion workseed, which develops the game, and they document the format. Why: contributors and operators need to know where development happens.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given backend/README.md, when it is read, then it says Worldseed holds the game, contribution intake and round lifecycle, and that development is done by devion workseed
- Given backend/docs/handoff.md, when it is read, then it documents the keys version, world_id, round_id, contributions, id, author, content and created_at and states that only frozen contributions are exported
- Given the docs, when they are read, then they contain no mention of worker, ExecutionPanel, Claude Code or Cursor


## Scope
- In scope: backend/README.md
- In scope: backend/docs/handoff.md
- Out of scope: Code changes
- Out of scope: Root README
- Preserve: Export format v1


## Technical constraints
- The documented format must match export.go exactly
- The docs must not claim a CLI or API for export that does not exist


## Definition of done
- Both docs are written and match the export type


## Clarifying questions
- None

# Worldseed backend

Worldseed keeps the game, the contribution intake and the round lifecycle. Frozen contributions are handed off to devion workseed, which develops the game. See [docs/handoff.md](docs/handoff.md).
steps.expected: README names devion workseed and links to the handoff doc.

steps.action: Create the doc. Describe Exporter.Export(ctx, worldID, roundID) in internal/contribution, which includes only contributions whose ids are frozen in the Round snapshot, in snapshot order, with an empty list when none exist. Include the version 1 JSON example with keys version, world_id, round_id and contributions[id, author, content, created_at as RFC 3339]. State that consumers check version first and that devion workseed is the consumer.
steps.expected: The doc exists and matches the Export struct tags.
